question.problem: The axis of symmetry of the parabola $y=-(x+7)(2x-5)$ is $x=${{field-1}}.
question.worked_solution:
From the equation $y=-(x+7)(2x-5),$ we find that the roots of the parabola are ${x}_{1}=-7$ and ${x}_{2}=\frac{5}{2}.$ 

To find the axis of symmetry, we take the average of the roots, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}x & =\frac{{x}_{1}+{x}_{2}}{2} \\  & =\frac{(-7+\frac{5}{2})}{2} \\  & =\frac{(-\frac{14}{2}+\frac{5}{2})}{2} \\  & =\frac{(-\frac{9}{2})}{2} \\  & =-\frac{9}{4}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the axis of symmetry is $x=-\frac{9}{4}.$
